documents.title: Artificial intelligence resources for faculty
documents.stance_why: The page tells faculty to "define permitted and prohibited use in your courses" and offers three sample statements ("All use ... permitted", "Limited use", "No use"), so the university sets no stance itself and delegates with tiers.
tiers: All use of generative AI is permitted, with acknowledgment
Limited use of generative AI is permitted in specific contexts
No use of generative AI tools permitted
documents.summary: Provost guidance for faculty: write syllabus statements using three sample tiers, do not mandate AI, treat detector output as non-definitive, and explore AI in courses. It also covers free Copilot and data cautions.

documents.title: AI and Acceptable Use
documents.stance_why: The page does not ban or hand off AI; it says AI use "is governed by" the existing acceptable use policy and sets conditions (use NAU credentials, no sensitive data in personal accounts, stay accountable), so it permits with conditions.
documents.summary: ITS page placing AI under the existing Appropriate Use policy with four principles: human accountability, NAU credentials and data protection, respect for privacy and IP, and efficient use. It targets staff and IT use more than coursework.
